latest_release.name: raea 0.1.8
latest_release.body:
raea 0.1.8 makes raea on Windows work the way it does on a Mac. Your AI agents install and connect, a phone's or a camera's video plays, the local models set themselves up with nothing installed first, the app draws on every kind of graphics card, and the installer asks where raea goes. It also exports your edit as layers for CapCut, Premiere Pro and DaVinci Resolve, has agents label what they show you, and makes the app lighter and quicker.

**Get the app at [raea.io](https://raea.io)** (a Mac with Apple silicon, Windows 10 or 11, or Linux on x86_64).

The engine alone:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raea.io/install | sh
```

On Windows, in PowerShell: `irm https://raea.io/install.ps1 | iex`.

## What changed since 0.1.7

**raea on Windows works.**
- Nothing needs installing first, and nothing has to download. The app carries what raea needs from outside it: Git, FFmpeg, uv (which sets up the local models) and Microsoft's Visual C++ runtime, so it works on a work PC that blocks downloads. Before, raea.exe wouldn't start without the Visual C++ Redistributable, and a workspace couldn't be made without Git.
- ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, OpenCode and Kimi install and connect on a Windows PC.
- The app calls your PC a PC: Ctrl, not ⌘, everywhere, the whiteboard too.
- The installer asks where raea goes. It suggests a folder in your own profile, takes any empty folder you can write to (or the folder raea is already in), and says why it won't use one that already holds other files. An update goes where the last install went, and uninstalling removes raea's own files and nothing else.
- The app draws on every kind of graphics card. On a PC with Intel or AMD graphics, including a laptop with AMD graphics beside an NVIDIA card, raea draws with DirectX 12. Before, the app could crash at launch on those (#155) and on Intel's integrated graphics. 3D on DirectX 12 is now drawn as on a Mac; with `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12` set by hand, 0.1.7 drew a scene's shapes into one another.
- A phone's or a camera's video plays, probes and checks. raea's own decoders read H.264 without B-frames, which is what raea writes, and the FFmpeg in the app reads the rest (most phone and camera footage: H.264 with B-frames, HEVC, VP9). It's built from FFmpeg's own source with no GPL part (FFmpeg's code and libvpx's decoders, for WebM with transparency), so its licence is the LGPL, and its source is published beside raea's releases. A clip raea cuts for you to play, such as `raea notes check`'s, uses Windows' own H.264 encoder. With raea from the zip and no FFmpeg on the PC, raea fetches the same build once and checks it before use.
- Agents' npm tools and MCP servers start without a shell, and their arguments arrive as written in folders with spaces or letters outside ASCII.
- Workspaces work (#169). raea wrote Windows' `\\?\` form of a folder's path into a workspace's `.git/config`, so every Git command in it failed and the app couldn't finish its first run, and a workspace's folder came out doubled when `raea.root` wasn't set. On a PC whose only Git is the app's, or none at all, `raea workspace`, `project` and `controller` use the app's Git or Git for Windows, or fetch raea's own once.
- The app no longer crashes at launch with a stack overflow (#112, #124). Its page host has the 8 MB stack it has on a Mac, and turns a file's bytes into text a piece at a time.
- What your agent runs through raea understands Windows. `raea show` finds the app wherever the installer put it, starts it, opens files in Explorer, and no longer says it opened them "in the Mac's own viewer". `raea init`, `show`, `cut` and `brand` take `C:\` and `\\server\share` paths, which they used to treat as relative ones.
- Numbers, money and dates format on Windows and Linux. `toLocaleString` and `Intl` in a composition threw "Intl is not defined" there; they now give the Mac's answers, in English and 40 other languages.
- `--quality master` keeps a dark background that changes slowly, such as a glow drifting

detail.readme:
raea

Render Anything Engine (for Anyone)

Tell your AI what to make. Videos, motion graphics, 3D and games, written as React and TypeScript
(the code your AI already writes) and rendered on your own GPU, faster than they play.

raea.io · Made in raea · Why raea · Docs · Releases

--- > **0.1.6** (17 November 2026) is the latest release: the engine and the desktop app on macOS (Apple Silicon), Linux > (x86_64) and, newest and least tested, Windows 10 and 11 (x86_64). raea is young and moves fast, with a release most > days since 0.1.1 on 11 November: expect rough edges, and tell us what you hit in an > [issue](https://github.com/shinyobjectz/raea/issues), or from your agent with `raea bug`. ## The app The raea app is where you make video, 3D and games with your AI. You ask in a chat; your own AI (Claude, ChatGPT, Kimi or a local model) writes the raea code and renders it; what it makes lands in the project's feed, where you watch it, scrub it, mark it up and send it back with notes. Download it from [raea.io](https://raea.io) for the Mac, Windows or Linux. It tells you when a new version is out; on the Mac it updates itself.

New to the app? **[Watch the tutorial](https://media.raea.io/#goose-learns-raea)** (5:50). What the app does now: - **The chat comes first** (0.1.5): your projects in a rail, the conversation in the middle, and `/goal` to keep an agent going until a condition you set holds. - **A timeline you edit by hand** (0.1.4): trim, split and move clips, speed curves, freeze frames and keys, the way CapCut works, under every film, sound and scene. - **Scenes you walk around in** (0.1.3): your agent posts a 3D scene and you walk through it, pin comments in it and move its parts by hand; every change is written into the scene's own code. - **Index** (0.1.5): your folders, drives and Apple Photos made searchable by what's in them, on your Mac. On an M5 Pro, 10,000 pictures were searchable in under a minute. - **Review** (0.1.6): each project has a Review tab, every comment you leave reaches the agent, and export is one window. - **Lighter** (0.1.6): the window gives back memory it's finished with and rests when nothing changes, 34% less CPU at rest. The app and the engine are free. Pro adds cloud storage, search across your computers and publishing; Team puts up to five people on one plan ([pricing](https://raea.io/pricing/)). Each release's notes are on the [releases page](https://github.com/shinyobjectz/raea/releases). ## Install ```sh curl -fsSL https://raea.io/install | sh ``` The installer puts the `raea` command under `~/.raea`, links it into `~/.local/bin`, and adds raea's agent skills to `~/.claude/skills`, so Claude Code (or any agent that reads that folder) knows how to write, render and check raea work. Run it again to update. The engine is free and needs no account. Tarballs and checksums are on the [releases page](https://github.com/shinyobjectz/raea/releases). On Windows 10 or 11, in PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://raea.io/install.ps1 | iex ``` It does the same under `~\.raea` and adds raea to your PATH. raea needs a DirectX 12 or Vulkan GPU driver; what else it needs (the Visual C++ runtime, FFmpeg and uv) is in its `bin\` folder. ## Hello A composition is a React component that draws a frame for a given moment: ```tsx import { AbsoluteFill, Composition, interpolate, registerRoot, useCurrentFrame } from "raea"; function Hello() { const f = useCurrentFrame(); return Hello; } registerRoot(() => ); ``` ```sh raea render hello.tsx -o hello.mp4 ``` On an Apple Silicon Mac those 90 frames render in about a second. The same file can play live as a game (`raea play`), render one frame for an agent to look at (`-o frame.png --frame 45`), or be checked against a quality floor (`raea check hello.mp4`). `raea init` starts a project, and `raea --help` lists every verb. ## What it does - **Video and motion graphics.** Layout, text, Tailwind, SVG and animation, composited on the GPU and encoded in hardware where the machine has it. Footage is cut by what's said in it (`raea cut`), and `raea check` catches clipped text, low contrast, unsafe areas, freezes and loudness problems before anyone watches. - **Games.** Input, physics, sound and 3D, played live with `raea play`, and exported as a program of their own (`raea export-game`). - **3D.** Scenes in TypeScript drawn by [Bevy](https://bevyengine.org) 0.20: cameras, lights, materials, glTF models, Gaussian splats, and Bevy plugins compiled into the engine. three.js work runs as it's written: a React Three Fiber scene inside ``, or a three.js page's script inside ``. - **Sound.** One mixer for live play and offline render, instruments and effects, and local models for foley and instrument notes (`raea sao`, `raea tokensynth`). - **Built for agents.** Everything it draws stays queryable as data, so an agent can render a frame, look at it, and fix what's wrong without a person in the loop. ## Made in raea Films, music videos, a tutorial and a game made with raea are on [media.raea.io](https://media.raea.io). Six of them come with their source in [raea-films](https://github.com/shinyobjectz/raea-films): each project's code under Apache-2.0, to read, render and take apart, and its models, textures and sound for anyone with a free raea account. ## Use it from your agent - **Agent skills.** They live in [raea-skills](https://github.com/shinyobjectz/raea-skills), pinned here as [`skills/`](skills): `raea` teaches an agent to write, render and check raea compositions, 3D and games included. The installer adds it to `~/.claude/skills`, and `raea skills install --agent NAME` to other agents. - **Claude plugin.** The raea skill and two hooks (raea's quick check after a composition is saved, and media shown in the raea app). In Claude Code: `/plugin install raea --marketplace shinyobjectz/raea-skills`. It's the `skills/` folder of raea-skills, and `/plugin marketplace add shinyobjectz/raea` installs the same one. - **Craft guides.** `raea guide` prints the floor every edit is held to and the guides for pitches, explainers, stories, games, motion, music and layout. `raea context PROJECT` says what to read before working on a project. - **Bug reports.** When an agent finds a bug in raea itself, `raea bug TITLE --text TEXT` sends it to raea's server with raea's version and the OS, no account needed. It sends words only: paths, emails and keys are taken out before it goes, and `--dry-run` prints what would go. ## Build from source Requirements: [Rust](https://rustup.rs) (rustup reads the pinned version from rust-toolchain.toml), [bun](https://bun.sh) and CMake. On macOS, Xcode's command-line tools; on Linux, the ALSA, fontconfig, udev, xkbcommon (with its X11 part, which the app targets' windows also load at run time) and Vulkan libraries and NASM (Ubuntu: `cmake ninja-build nasm libasound2-dev libfontconfig1-dev libudev-dev libvulkan-dev libxkbcommon-dev libxkbcommon-x11-dev`), as public CI installs them. ```sh git clone https://github.com/shinyobjectz/raea && cd raea cargo build --release -p raea-cli --no-default-features for d in sdk/raea sdk/react/js sdk/react/tw; do (cd $d && bun install); done target/release/raea render sdk/react/bench/games/pong/edit.tsx -o pong.mp4 ``` `--no-default-features` builds the public engine, as the releases are. The default features add one hosted service, Content Credentials signed by raea's signing server, which isn't part of this repository. raea sends nothing on its own: no telemetry, crash reports or update checks. What reaches the network is what you ask for (a remote URL in a composition, a model downloaded on first use, a `raea gen` step on a provider you hold a key for), and `RAEA_OFFLINE=1` refuses all of it. [docs/settings.md](docs/settings.md) lists the settings raea reads. ## What's in here The workspace is layered, from pure building blocks up to the command. | Folder | What | |---|---| | [`core/`](core) | Pure building blocks: the kernel language (K, interpreted on the CPU and compiled to WGSL), easing and animation, shapes, fonts, the scene and wire formats | | [`gpu/`](gpu) | The one shared GPU device and its telemetry | | [`io/`](io) | Decode and encode (VideoToolbox, software codecs, AV1, a muxer), files, network, npm packages, traces | | [`systems/`](systems) | Engine systems: layout, canvas, compositing, filters, mixing, speech, ML on ONNX Runtime, footage reading, lighting, contact checks for 3D parts, splats | | [`runtime/`](runtime) | Running a composition: the JavaScript engine seam (JavaScriptCore on macOS, QuickJS elsewhere), React and HTML on Bevy, baking, encode, live play | | [`engine/`](engine) | The renderer (`engine/render`), the in-process TypeScript bundler, the Bevy plugin catalog, and the `raea` command itself (`engine/cli`) | | [`apps/`](apps) | The crates behind the CLI's verbs: check, play, games, media | | [`sdk/`](sdk) | `raea`, the TypeScript SDK (`sdk/raea`), its 3D, physics, audio, video and UI packages, the craft guides, and the agent skills | | [`vendor/`](vendor) | Patched upstream crates, under their own licences ([`vendor/vendor.toml`](vendor/vendor.toml) says why each is patched) | | [`tools/`](tools) | Build and release helpers | Behaviour specs written in Gherkin (`.feature`) sit beside the code they describe. ## Licence raea is under the [Functional Source License 1.1, ALv2 Future License](LICENSE) (FSL-1.1-ALv2), copyright Shane Murphy. Use it, change it, build on it and pass it on for anything except a product that competes with raea. Each version becomes Apache-2.0 two years after its release. Third-party parts keep their own licences; see [NOTICE](NOTICE).
